decision: Approve supplied target artifact readability and passive local rendering, with explicit browser-wide networking and print-pagination limits

desktop.assessment: Clear hierarchy and readable literal message bodies after author/ID/date and before secondary metadata. Unicode and supplied markup-looking text remain visible; no clipping/overlap observed.

narrow.assessment: Single-column fact rows, long metadata/URLs and download label wrap within the viewport; body-first placement remains clear. No horizontal clipping/overlap observed.

print.assessment: All four pages inspected. Bodies, Unicode, metadata and footer are readable and retained; download/back controls are suppressed. Page2 has substantial blank area before first-message metadata continues on page3; page4 is sparse. This is a nonblocking pagination inefficiency, not content loss. No source edit proposed.

rendered_body_values: Both actual DOM body text values exactly match decoded-source JSON at desktop, narrow and print media; original LF/tab/Unicode retained.

browser_wide_networking.limits: Actual browser startup/background URL jobs and UDP socket checks occurred despite disabling flags. Target offline mode is not proof of whole-browser network silence. No OS packet capture/isolation claim; no successful outside HTTP transaction is evidenced by this netlog.

publication_redaction: The exact isolated-run netlog stays native. Archive contains a deterministic HTTP(S) query-value-redacted copy plus raw hash and redaction receipt; key/cup2 query values are never printed or published.
preservation: Original frozen driver, initial socket-path failure, corrected receiver, original source review and body-first source review retained. Supplied HTML and receiver unchanged. No source edits, maintained-test replay or third browser attempt.
scope_limits: One authored synthetic conversation and one installed browser, not live school/account receiving, all browser/font/OS coverage, accessibility certification, or universal print-pagination proof.
